messages:
marta: quick one — ran into a surprising behavior in the python sample app when using async stream_tool_call with backpressure. if the tool is slow we end up buffering a lot and the app OOMs.

marta: sample usage in the repro:

marta: ```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
from dataclasses import dataclass
client = AsyncClient(api_key="...")

@dataclass
class Hit:
    id: str
    score: float

# stream_tool_call yields an async iterator of Hit
async for item in client.stream_tool_call(
    "search_stream", input={"q": "redwood"}, output_type=Hit,
):
    process(item)  # downstream slow consumer
```

marta: when process() is slow the SDK keeps pulling frames from transport and buffering parsed items. we'd expect some sort of request-level backpressure or a max_buffer config.

liam: yep, streaming over HTTP/WS is tricky. by default the transport will push frames as they arrive. we should offer an option to pause reading from socket until the consumer iterates (i.e., apply flow-control).

zhen: related: typing ergonomics — stream_tool_call currently types as AsyncIterator[Any] in stubs which confuses users. Would be nice to have AsyncIterator[Hit] when output_type provided. Also need a sync-friendly wrapper that returns an iterator for sync code.

marta: another gotcha: when we apply backpressure via a semaphore in the client, the server still keeps sending and the buffer grows on the socket layer. so we need to coordinate lower-level read, not just our parse queue.

liam: implementation ideas:
- expose stream_tool_call(..., max_inflight=16, read_strategy='block'|'drain') where 'block' will not read additional frames from the transport when in-flight parsed items >= max_inflight (requires pausing the underlying reader).
- add max_buffer_bytes and drop_policy options (drop-oldest, raise, block) for safety.
- provide typed stubs: `async def stream_tool_call(..., output_type: Type[T]) -> AsyncIterator[T]` in pyi. and a sync helper `def stream_tool_call_sync(...)-> Iterator[T]` that wraps the async iterator for sample apps that run in sync tests.

zhen: for tests, we need a deterministic fake transport that simulates a fast producer / slow consumer and asserts we never exceed max_buffer_bytes. Also test abort semantics: if consumer cancels iteration early, we must cancel the in-flight stream and close socket.

marta: small UX ask: sample-apps and quickstart show streaming simple prints. we should add a "production streaming" recipe that demonstrates max_inflight, backpressure, and cancellation. Customers copy the simple example into production and hit memory spikes.

liam: another typing request: support AsyncIterator[Union[Hit, ErrorEvent]] where ErrorEvent is a typed parse error for partially malformed items. Users can choose to receive parse errors inline instead of exceptions. i'd model it as a StreamItem union: either parsed or parse_error metadata. This is useful for noisy external tools.

zhen: good idea. maybe: StreamItem[T] = Union[T, StreamParseError], and pyi would reflect AsyncIterator[StreamItem[T]] when include_parse_errors=True. Keep default as AsyncIterator[T] with exceptions.

marta: logging snippet from failing customer shows buffer growth: 

marta: ```
DEBUG transport frame recv size=8192
DEBUG parsed items queued=1024 memory=120MB
WARNING consumer slow, applying client-side queueing
ERROR memory exceeded, crash
```

liam: plan:
1) add options: max_inflight, max_buffer_bytes, read_strategy, include_parse_errors
2) implement pausable reader on our websocket/http2 transport (awaitable pause()/resume())
3) pyi updates for typed AsyncIterator[T] and StreamItem union support
4) docs: add production streaming recipe and sample server that simulates slow consumer

zhen: I'll own the pyi/typing changes. martA can add the sample-app recipe and tests. liam can do the transport pause/resume and unit tests with fake transport.

docbot: created issue redwood/sdk#3801 "python sdk: stream_tool_call backpressure controls, typed async iterator, and parse-error streaming" (assigned to @liam). https://github.com/redwood/sdk/issues/3801

qa-bot: added test ticket QA-1222 for integration validation: scenarios: fast-producer/slow-consumer, consumer cancel mid-stream, include_parse_errors toggled, max_buffer_bytes enforcement.

marta: thanks all. i'll add a short repro in repro-examples and link the customer trace in the issue. ping me for reviews. :thumbsup:
